assessment: Chemically fixing cells for fluorescence microscopy is a common practice in cell biology. However, fixation artifacts can lead the incorrect interpretations of experimental results. This article presents compelling evidence showing that in the context of liquid condensates formed by liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS), paraformaldehyde (PFA) fixation creates a number of artifacts – such as changes in the number, appearance, or disappearance of liquid condensates. These important findings will be of great interest not only for those in the LLPS field but for any cell biologists using fixed samples for microscopy.
